 Judgment

1. This appeal is filed challenging the order passed by under section 54 of the Land Acquisition Act read with section 96 of the Code of Civil Procedure challenging the judgment and award dated 12.04.2012 passed by learned 4th Additional Senior Civil Judge, Mehsana in NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/408/2026 JUDGMENT DATED: 03/03/2026 undefined LAR No.233/2008 arising from common order in LAR 230/2008 to 270/2008 (main LAR No.230/2008) whereby learned reference court has determined the additional compensation of the land acquired of village Saduthala at the rate of Rs.134/- per sq.mtr.
2.

At the outset, learned advocate Mr.Rakesh Patel submits that this appeal is left out from the group which was decided by this court and rendered judgment on 24.01.2025 and at the end this Court has remanded back the matter to the learned reference court for determining the fresh market value on the basis of additional evidence which are placed on record by the learned advocate Mr.Patel.
In that background, learned advocate Mr.Rakesh Patel submits that identical order is required to be passed in the present appeal herein and matter is required to be remanded back.

3. Per contra, learned AGP Ms.Himani Shah does not dispute with regard to the above aspect and has submitted to pass appropriate order.
4.

Considering the submissions, this Court has referred the decision render by this Court in first appeal no.3913/2024 wherein it is held as under:
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/408/2026 JUDGMENT DATED: 03/03/2026 undefined "7.
Having heard the learned advocates appearing for the respective parties and having perused the impugned judgment and award.

Considering the facts of the present case and the averments made in the application seeking production of additional documents, indisputedly, the prima facie reading of the documents produced on record in the civil application, it transpires that the lands of Visnagar are acquired for the same project as in case of the lands of village Saduthala.

The drawing sketch of Saduthala as well as Visnagar sim has been relied upon which seems to be issued by the Deputy Executive Engineer, Dharoi Canal Sub-division No.6 as produced on record at Annexure-A.

While considering the aspect of best exemplar available on record, the Courts are expected to primarily consider two factors, which is, proximity of time line of issuance of Section 4 notification and the proximity of distance between two instances.

As far as Section 4 notification is concerned, indisputedly, it is evident from the reading of the judgment as produced on record at Annexure-A to the civil application seeking NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/408/2026 JUDGMENT DATED: 03/03/2026 undefined production of additional documents in case of LAR Case Nos.352/2009 to 387/2009 & 3561/2011 in case of Visnagar, is of 18.07.2002, whereas, for the lands acquired in the present case at village Saduthala, the date of Section 4 notification is 02.08.2002, which is 14 days from the date of the notification issued in the case of Visnagar sim.
Thus, there is hardly difference of few days in the aforesaid two notifications.

sentences.text: Secondly, it is also evident that the lands have been acquired for the same public purpose i.e for SIPU Yojna.

The prima facie reading of the sketch produced on record at Annexure-B issued by the Deputy Executive Engineer, Dharoi Canal Sub-division No.6, Vadnagar as indicated by the learned advocate, the lands acquired seems to be the part of the same channel.

Thus, a prima facie case is made out to believe the contention of the claimants that as compared to the instance relied upon by the Reference Court at Exh.-10, 11 and 32, the instance proposed to be relied upon at Annexure-A situated immediately to the lands acquired of village Saduthala, however, the aforesaid contention raised NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/408/2026 JUDGMENT DATED: 03/03/2026 undefined by the original claimants is required to be strictly examined after recording the evidence.
In the opinion of this Court, the matter deserves consideration.

The ultimate object of the Land Acquisition Act and looking to the scheme of the Act, it is not only restricted to expedite the law for the acquisition of the lands needed for public purpose but, at the same time, it also aims to determine the amount of compensation to be made on account of such acquisition.

The very fact that Section 18 confers right upon aggrieved party to prefer a reference against the amount determined by the Special Land Acquisition Officer under Section 11 of the Act, is to determine correct amount of compensation.

Section 18 of the Act, 1894 reads thus :
18. Reference to Court (1) Any person interested who has not accepted the award may, by written application to the Collector, require that the matter be referred by the Collector for the determination of the Court, whether his objection be to the measurement of the land, the amount of the compensation, the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/408/2026 JUDGMENT DATED: 03/03/2026 undefined persons to whom it is payable, or the apportionment of the compensation among the persons interested.
(2) The application shall state the grounds on which objection to the award is taken:
Provided that every such application shall be made,
(a) if the person making it was present or represented before the Collector at the time when he made his award, within six weeks from the date of the Collectors award;
(b) in other cases, within six weeks of the receipt of the notice from the Collector under section 12, sub-section (2), or within six months from the date of the Collectors award, whichever period shall first expire.
8.

On overall consideration of the additional documents in light of the provisions of Section 18 of the Act, 1894, keeping in mind the object of the Act to provide just and fair compensation, in the opinion of this Court, the appellants are entitled to have a fair chance to prove their reference for reconsideration for limited purpose.

Hence, the matters are remanded NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/408/2026 JUDGMENT DATED: 03/03/2026 undefined back to the Reference Court to examine the aforesaid contention of the original claimants by extending them an opportunity to produce the aforesaid two documents as produced on record in the application seeking production of additional documents.

The Reference Court is directed to examine the aforesaid issue and to Legal Heirs Of Deceased Patel ... vs State Of Gujarat on 3 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126634908/
3 determine the correct amount of compensation strictly in accordance with law.

The impugned judgment and award passed by the Reference Court is hereby quashed and set aside."
5.
Undisputedly, these matters are left out from the above groups therefore, identical order is required to be passed.

The present first appeal is disposed of with following directions:
6. The Reference Court shall take into consideration the aforesaid order, while determining the additional amount of compensation.
It is clarified that all the rights and contentions of the respective parties are kept open and this Court has not opined on entitlement of enhanced compensation.
With this observation all the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/408/2026 JUDGMENT DATED: 03/03/2026 undefined First Appeals stand disposed of in aforesaid terms.
No order as to costs.
It is clarified that the claimant would not be entitled for the interest qua delayed period i.e from the date of order passed by learned reference court till the date of filing of the appeal.
7. Record and Proceedings, if, called for are directed to be sent back forthwith.
